Module 1: Poor Personal Hygiene & Staff.Description: Employees perform full 20-second handwashing with soap and running warm water at required intervals.
ABSOLUTELY ZERO bare-hand contact with Ready-to-Eat (RTE) foods; dedicated clean utensils or gloves used.
Handwashing sinks are dedicated exclusively for hand hygiene, fully accessible, and unobstructed.
Hand sinks continuously stocked with antibacterial liquid soap, single-use paper towels/dryer, and trash bin with lid.
Employee health reporting policy documented and enforced; staff can articulate reportable symptoms.
Strict exclusion enforced: No staff working with jaundice, diarrhea, vomiting, or communicable illness (Valid LGU Health Cards).
Open cuts/wounds covered with high-visibility waterproof blue detectable bandages AND covered with single-use glove.
Clean uniforms, protective aprons, and closed-toe slip-resistant footwear worn; aprons removed before restroom/breaks.
Effective hair restraints (caps/nets) and beard snoods worn by all food handlers, enclosing hair completely.
Fingernails kept trimmed short, clean, and free of nail polish, artificial nails, decals, or acrylics.
Strict zero-jewelry policy enforced (only single plain wedding band allowed; zero watches, rings, piercings).
Personal items, cell phones, bags, medication, and street apparel stored strictly in employee lockers.
Eating, drinking, vaping, or tobacco use strictly restricted to designated employee break areas.
Clear, visible handwashing signage (bilingual/graphical) posted at all handwashing sinks and restrooms.
Food hygiene and sanitation training records available on-site; staff trained on cross-contamination and hygiene.

Module 2: Improper Holding Temperature &.Description: Cold holding: All TCS foods maintained strictly at ≤ 41°F (5°C) across storage and display.
Hot holding: TCS foods maintained continuously at ≥ 135°F (57°C) [or ≥ 140°F / 60°C per local standards].
Two-Stage Cooling enforced: Cooled from 135°F to 70°F in 2 hrs, and to ≤ 41°F within next 4 hrs (≤ 6 hrs total).
Chiller walk-ins and reach-in refrigeration units maintain ambient air temperature at ≤ 38°F (3.3°C).
Commercial freezers maintain frozen food rock-solid; ambient air maintained at ≤ 0°F (-18°C) without excessive ice.
Accurate, conspicuous external/internal ambient thermometers installed in all cooling and freezing units.
Internal food temperatures of stored TCS items and holding wells verified and logged at minimum 4-hour intervals.
Cooling logs identify batch IDs, start/end times, temperatures, and rapid-chilling methods used.
Buffet lines, salad bars, banchan wells, raw yakiniku display trays systematically monitored for temperature.
TPHC Protocol: Foods held without temperature control labeled with 4-hr discard time and discarded promptly.
Thawing conducted exclusively under refrigeration (≤ 41°F), continuous cold running potable water (≤ 70°F), or cooking.
ABSOLUTELY ZERO food observed thawing at ambient room temperature, in stagnant water pools, or on kitchen floors.
Daily temperature logs reviewed, verified, and signed off by the FSCO or shift supervisor daily.
Proper cold airflow maintained: Storage shelves not overstocked; foods arranged to permit air circulation.
Documented emergency contingency SOP exists for temperature deviation during power outages or unit breakdown.

Module 3: Inadequate Cooking, Thermal Le.Description: Poultry, wild game, and stuffed meats reach minimum internal core temperature of ≥ 165°F (74°C) for 15 seconds.
Ground beef, minced pork reach minimum internal core temperature of ≥ 155°F (68°C) for 15 seconds (or ≥ 70°C).
Whole seafood, fish fillets, intact pork/beef cuts reach minimum internal core temperature of ≥ 145°F (63°C) for 15 sec.
Reheating previously cooked TCS foods for hot holding reaches ≥ 165°F (74°C) across product within 2 hours.
Digital probe thermometers with fine-tip sensors available at every cook station and sanitized prior to measurement.
Clear Consumer Advisory present on menus for customer-ordered raw/undercooked animal proteins.
Cooking CCP logs reflect actual measured core temperatures with exact timestamps (not fabricated/estimated).
Microwave cooking: Food covered, rotated/stirred halfway through, and stood for 2 minutes to equilibrate at ≥ 165°F.
Large roasts and slow-cooked braises comply with validated time-temperature lethality tables.
Batch cooking and timed replenishment utilized to prevent thermal abuse and excessive holding times.
Specialized processes (Sous-vide, Cook-Chill, ROP) operate with validated HACCP plans and continuous data loggers.
Probe thermometer accuracy verified weekly using Ice-Water Slurry (32°F ± 1°F) and Boiling Water (212°F ± 1°F).
Raw/RTE high-risk specialties (sushi-grade fish, oysters) follow dedicated microbial/thermal destruction SOPs.
ABSOLUTELY NO double-reheating: Leftover or reheated TCS foods held in hot wells are never cooled and reheated again.
Line cooks and station leaders can articulate the exact validated critical limit / Kill Step for their station.

Module 4: Cross-Contamination & Allergen.Description: Raw animal proteins strictly stored below Ready-to-Eat (RTE) foods, produce, and cooked foods in storage.
Vertical hierarchy: Top: RTE/Produce → 2nd: Fish/Seafood → 3rd: Whole Beef/Pork → 4th: Ground Meats → Bottom: Poultry.
Color-coded cutting boards/knives actively used (Red: Meat, Yellow: Poultry, Blue: Seafood, Green: Produce, White: RTE, Purple: Allergen).
Staff change gloves, wash hands, and sanitize cutting boards immediately when transitioning raw proteins to RTE.
Major Allergens (Big 9) identified; cross-contact controls implemented across all prep steps.
Dedicated, color-coded Allergen prep utensils (purple boards/tongs) maintained, stored separately, and sanitized.
Raw fruits, vegetables, salad greens washed in dedicated sanitized prep sink (using approved produce wash).
First-In, First-Out (FIFO) and FEFO rotation strictly maintained across all dry storage and walk-in coolers.
All stored food containers sealed and labeled with product name, prep/opening date, and calculated expiration date.
Food and ingredient containers stored minimum 6 inches (15 cm) above floor on clean, rust-free shelving.
Product expiration dates and supplier Use-By / Best Before dates are never altered, overwritten, or re-stickered.
In-use wiping cloths stored completely submerged in clean sanitizer buckets (Chlorine 50-100 ppm / Quat 200 ppm).
Food tasting conducted strictly using Two-Spoon method or single-use spoons; no double-dipping.
Sneeze guards and breath protectors on buffets and display cases are fully functional, clean, and intact.
Customer table cooking (Hotpot, Samgyupsal) provides separate distinct tongs for raw meat handling vs. cooked eating.

Module 5: Food from Unsafe Sources & Tra.Description: All food ingredients, meats, seafood sourced strictly from licensed, authorized, government-approved suppliers.
Incoming refrigerated TCS items received at ≤ 41°F (5°C); frozen products received rock-solid at ≤ 0°F (-18°C).
Receiving logbook systematically records lot numbers, supplier names, vehicle temperatures, and product core temps.
Shellstock identification tags for molluscan shellfish retained chronologically on-site for 90 days minimum.
Parasite destruction letters and freezing logs on file for all raw/marinated fish served for RTE/sushi service.
Packaging integrity: Canned/packaged goods inspected upon delivery; free of dents, rust, bloating, or seal breaches.
Custom-processed meats, cured proteins, acidified rice have required regulatory variances/HACCP authorizations.
Shell eggs received clean, undamaged, with grade markings, and immediately refrigerated at ≤ 45°F (7.2°C).
Milk, liquid dairy, cheeses, and egg products are pasteurized with valid manufacturer expiration dates.
Delivery vehicles inspected for cleanliness, lack of pest activity, absence of hazardous chemicals, and temp control.
Damaged, off-temp, or expired goods rejected immediately or clearly marked and placed in a locked Quarantined Area.
Dry goods inspected for signs of moisture, insect larvae, webbing, or rodent damage upon delivery.
Annual supplier compliance reviews conducted: Certificates of Analysis (COA), LGU/NMIS accreditations verified.
Strict emergency sourcing SOP enforced: Prohibits unauthorized, unvetted market purchases without FSCO clearance.
Commercial canned goods: Zero presence of swollen, leaking, deeply dented seams, or severely rusted cans.

Module 6: Contaminated Equipment, Sanita.Description: Mechanical dishwashers meet specs: Wash temp ≥ 150°F-160°F; final sanitizing rinse reaches ≥ 180°F (surface ≥ 160°F).
Sanitizing concentration (Chlorine 50-100 ppm, Quat 200-400 ppm) actively verified hourly with chemical test strips.
Food-contact surfaces and prep tables are smooth, non-porous, corrosion-resistant, and free of deep grooves.
Mechanical slicers, grinders, and blenders are completely dismantled, washed, and sanitized at least every 4 hours.
Commercial can openers and immersion blenders have clean housings and blades free of metal shavings or debris.
Heavy kitchen equipment elevated at least 6 inches off the floor or sealed to floor/walls with food-grade silicone.
Probe thermometers and calibration tools sanitized with 70% alcohol wipes before and after food insertion.
Ice machine interior, water distribution tubes, and dispensing chutes are clean and free of biofilm, slime, or mold.
Exhaust hoods, baffles, and grease filters are clean, free of dripping grease, and degreased on regular schedule.
Storage shelving in walk-ins constructed of NSF stainless steel or epoxy-coated plastic; zero raw/unsealed wood.
Non-food contact surfaces (door handles, refrigerator gaskets, switch plates, casters) clean to sight and touch.
Cleaned dishware and smallwares completely inverted and air-dried on wire racks; strictly zero towel drying.
Three-Compartment sink sequence maintained: Sink 1 Wash (≥ 110°F) → Sink 2 Rinse → Sink 3 Sanitize.
Cleaned utensils and cutlery stored handles-up in clean organizers to prevent touch contamination.
Master Cleaning Schedule (MCS) visibly posted, covering frequencies, chemicals, procedures, and staff sign-offs.

Module 7: Water Quality, Plumbing & Grea.Description: Potable water supply tested annually (microbiological and physico-chemical per PNSDW) with accredited test certificates.
Plumbing system in sound working order; absolutely zero cross-connections, leaks, or back-siphonage risks.
Certified backflow preventers and vacuum breakers installed on all dishwashers, pre-rinse hoses, and dispensers.
Floor drains and trench drains clean, properly graded, equipped with removable strainer baskets, free of sewer odors.
Continuous supply of hot and cold potable water available under adequate pressure at all sinks and dish machines.
Beverage dispensers, ice machines, and espresso water systems equipped with inline filters replaced per schedule.
Sewage and liquid waste disposal complies with PD 856; zero sewage backups or wastewater floor seepage.
Overhead waste or sewer pipes in food zones sleeved or shielded; zero dripping or condensation.
Water heating systems provide continuous hot water at minimum 120°F (49°C) at manual warewashing sinks.
Grease traps inspected and cleaned on documented weekly schedule; grease disposal manifests archived on-site.
Sinks and drainage channels drain swiftly; zero standing wastewater or ponding observed on kitchen floors.
Bottled water and culinary ice sourced exclusively from FDA-registered, accredited water purification facilities.
Mop sinks and janitorial wash basins strictly separated from food prep sinks and equipped with vacuum breakers.
Overhead water storage cisterns/tanks hermetically sealed, access-controlled, and sanitized annually.
Documented Emergency Water Supply Plan and Boil Water Advisory SOP in place for municipal water disruption.

Module 8: Presence of Pests, Integrated.Description: Zero evidence of active rodent activity (droppings, rub marks, gnawing, urine stains, nesting) across premises.
Zero evidence of active cockroach, fly, or ant infestation in food preparation, storage, or dining areas.
Licensed Pest Control Operator (PCO) contract active; monthly service reports and chemical logs on file.
External building perimeter sealed: All doors, windows, pipe penetrations have zero gaps exceeding 1/4 inch (6 mm).
Screen doors intact; air curtains / fly fans installed over exterior entrances operate automatically upon opening.
Exterior delivery and customer entry doors remain tightly closed when not in use; self-closing devices functional.
Solid waste bins lined with heavy-duty bags, equipped with tight-fitting lids, and emptied frequently.
External dumpster area is paved, graded away from building, clean, free of runoff, and lids kept closed.
Absolute zero presence of live animals, domestic pets, birds, or pests within food storage and preparation zones.
Safety Data Sheets (SDS) and government registration certificates for all pest control chemicals archived on-site.
Exterior rodent bait stations are tamper-resistant, anchored, locked, and mapped accurately per PCO schematic.
Electronic fly traps / insect light traps positioned away from exposed food prep tables (never directly above food).
Dry storage shelving maintained with a minimum 12-inch (30 cm) inspection aisle away from perimeter walls.
Structural floors, wall junctions, and coving sealed with impervious, washable materials; zero pest harborage holes.
Exterior landscaping and foliage trimmed at least 18 inches away from walls; zero standing exterior water pools.
